title: Father, This Slumber Shake
description: Father, This Slumber Shake in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 515, “Watch and Pray, Lest Ye Enter into Temptation”, where the book credits them to Wesleyan.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, this slum-ber shake From off my hea-vy soul! Say to me now, a-wake! a-wake! And I will make thee whole!

lines: Say to me now, — awake! awake!
And I will make thee whole!
Give me on Thee to call;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
